subject: Copywriting
title: Lord Kitchener Wants You
description: A 60-second lesson on Lord Kitchener Wants You.

hook.text: A pointing finger and five words: 'Your Country Needs YOU.' The 1914 British poster recruited 2.5 million volunteers.

buildup.text: Alfred Leete designed the poster showing Lord Kitchener pointing directly at the viewer. It was personal and commanding.

discovery.text: The poster used second-person address—'YOU'—making each viewer feel personally called.

twist.text: The Americans copied it. James Montgomery Flagg painted Uncle Sam pointing: 'I Want YOU.' Same pose, same psychology.

climax.text: One poster format, two nations, millions of recruits.

punchline.text: One pointing finger, 2.5 million volunteers. Copy can mobilize nations.

quiz.question: How many volunteers did the Kitchener poster help recruit?
